messages:
Maria Chen: quick heads-up — SSO failures from Okta started ~09:12 PT. A bunch of users hitting 401 on our app. seeing 'SAMLResponse: invalid audience' in the logs :eyes:
Ash Patel: can you paste the actual saml error line?
Maria Chen: sure — from the ingress log: 
```
2026-03-21T16:12:08Z ERROR saml: validation failed: assertion audience mismatch: expected 'https://app.redwood.com' got 'https://redwood.app'
```
Jen Ford: we did the RBAC hostname normalization rollout yesterday morning — that changed the internal reverse-proxy host header mapping. could that have flipped the SP entityID when we generated new metadata? :thinking_face:
Alex Li: Also noticed SCIM provisioner created two service-account-ops users around the same time, both with different externalId values. likely the provisioning payload had a different identifier.
sec-bot: security-alert: KMS decrypt errors observed while loading idp certs: 
```
ERROR kms: decrypt failed: context mismatch for key alias projects/redwood/keys/idp-rotate-v2
```
ops-bot: started a quick metadata rollback to previous IdP metadata (v2026-03-19) to restore SSO while we triage. will post status in 2m. :rotating_light:
Ash Patel: initial hypothesis: IdP metadata update we imported used the old entityID (https://redwood.app) but our SP settings expect https://app.redwood.com. That would explain audience mismatch and the duplicated SCIM externalId if mapping used host-based values.
Maria Chen: we tested metadata import in staging but not prod — my bad. I pushed the console change to prod. I'll revert the entityID override immediately.
Jen Ford: who touched the RBAC hostname mapping? @people-ops can you check audit logs for a mapping change around 03/20 10:00 UTC? we need the operator and the exact config diff.
people-ops: pulled audit: mapping-change by 'jen.ford' at 2026-03-20T10:03:12Z — diff shows we replaced host alias list with canonical hostnames. attaching audit id: AUDIT-20260320-4321.
Alex Li: KMS context mismatch could be from the metadata import tool reading the wrong encryption context after the rollback. We rotated the idp key two weeks ago — maybe the metadata importer used the old context value.
Ash Patel: workaround: set SP to accept both entityIDs for a short window (https://redwood.app and https://app.redwood.com) and enable strict audience validation back off to warn-only. Not ideal, but buys us time.
Maria Chen: applied dual-entityID accept on the SP and configured warn-only for audience validation. Confirmed a handful of users can login now.
sec-bot: note — audit log shows the KMS operation that failed was a GetPublicKey call at 16:11:58Z followed by Decrypt at 16:12:07Z. Correlate with metadata import attempt.
ops-bot: rolling forward the correct IdP metadata (the one with canonical entityID) now; will coordinate with Ash to flip strict validation back on after KMS fix.
Ash Patel: I'll re-run the metadata import with explicit encryption-context param and check KMS logs. If decrypt still fails, escalate to cloud KMS team.
Jen Ford: after we stabilize, we should: 1) add an idempotent check in the metadata importer to block entityID regressions, 2) ensure SCIM provisioning uses immutable externalId (not host-derived), 3) add an automated canary that exercises login after metadata change.
Alex Li: +1 on immutable externalId. I can put a patch in the SCIM mapping to prefer stable uuid if present.
Maria Chen: thanks team. leaving a short postmortem stub in incidents channel. tagging folks to follow up on remediation items. :lock:
Ash Patel: quick action items I have: re-run import w/ context, validate KMS decrypt, confirm no lingering duplicates in SCIM queue, flip audience validation to strict after KMS ok.
people-ops: I'll attach audit entries and the config diff to the incident.
Maria Chen: closing thread for now, monitoring traffic — hit me if anyone sees repeat errors. :thumbsup:
